question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose plugin-authored AI-safety events, a `safetyEventTypes` manifest permission, durable shared-state retention, and operator-query surfaces as core contracts, or should this land as a narrower internal diagnostics seam first?
rationale: This is a lasting SDK, authorization, persistence, and operator-product boundary; source review can validate mechanics but cannot choose the intended public contract and support commitment.

options.title: Approve the complete core contract
options.body: Accept the plugin API, manifest permission, durable history, retention behavior, and operator surfaces as supported core functionality, then correct the remaining coverage documentation.

options.title: Land a narrower diagnostics foundation first
options.body: Keep only explicitly approved core emitters and exporter-facing internal diagnostics seams, deferring plugin emission, durable retention, and the broad UI/CLI surface to follow-up design work.

options.title: Decline this core direction
options.body: Keep the existing diagnostics model and route optional safety dashboards or integrations through plugins once a specific extension need is established.

recommendation.title: Land a narrower diagnostics foundation first
recommendation.body: Keep only explicitly approved core emitters and exporter-facing internal diagnostics seams, deferring plugin emission, durable retention, and the broad UI/CLI surface to follow-up design work.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion explicitly requests this person’s decision on the new plugin SDK and core product boundary.
